templates.let_rec: let rec {- name -} = {- value -} in {- body -}

exercise_01.name: Return a number
exercise_01.description: Write a single expression whose value is any integer. Just typing the number on its own line is a valid program.

exercise_02.name: Return true
exercise_02.description: Return the boolean [code]true[/code]. The starter code already has [code]true[/code] written for you — just remove the leading [code]--[/code] so it stops being a comment.

exercise_03.name: Return a tuple
exercise_03.description: Return any tuple. A tuple groups a fixed number of values written inside parentheses, separated by commas — for example [code](1, 2)[/code] or [code](true, 0, 99)[/code].

exercise_04.name: Return a list
exercise_04.description: Return any non-empty list of numbers. You can write the elements out by hand ([code][10, 20, 30][/code]) or use a range like [code][1..5][/code]. The [b]range[/b] template, just unlocked, gives you a head start.

exercise_05.name: Double a Number
exercise_05.description: Write a function that takes one argument and returns its double.

exercise_06.name: Add Two Numbers
exercise_06.description: Write a function that takes two arguments and returns their sum.

exercise_07.name: Square a Number
exercise_07.description: Write a function that returns the square of its input.

exercise_08.name: Sum of List
exercise_08.description: Write a function that returns the sum of a list of integers. Hint: use foldr or recursion.

exercise_09.name: Length of List
exercise_09.description: Write a function that returns the number of elements in a list.
